solved.q: A system absorbs 2000 J of heat and does 800 J of work on its surroundings. Find the change in internal energy of the system.
solved.ans: dU = 1200 J (internal energy increases by 1200 J)

solved.q: 2 moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally at 300 K from volume V to 2V. Find the work done by the gas. (R = 8.314 J/mol K, ln2 = 0.6931)
steps: Given: n = 2 mol, T = 300 K, V2/V1 = 2, R = 8.314 J/mol K.
Substitution: W = 2 x 8.314 x 300 x ln(2).

solved.q: In an adiabatic process a gas does 150 J of work on its surroundings. Find the change in its internal energy.
steps: Given: dW = 150 J (work done by gas), dQ = 0 (adiabatic).
Formula (first law for adiabatic process): dQ = dU + dW, with dQ = 0, so dU = -dW.
Calculation: dU = -150 J, i.e. internal energy decreases.
solved.ans: dU = -150 J (decrease of 150 J; temperature of gas falls)

solved.topic: Work done at constant pressure (area under P-V curve)
solved.q: A gas at a constant pressure of 1.5 x 10^5 Pa expands so that its volume changes from 1 x 10^-3 m^3 to 2.5 x 10^-3 m^3. Find the work done by the gas.
steps: Formula (isobaric work = area under P-V curve): W = P(V2 - V1).

solved.q: A heat engine absorbs 600 J of heat from the source and rejects 400 J to the sink in each cycle. Find the work done per cycle and the efficiency of the engine.
steps: Formula: W = Q1 - Q2 and efficiency eta = W/Q1.

solved.q: A Carnot engine operates between a source at 500 K and a sink at 300 K. If it absorbs 2000 J of heat from the source, find (i) its efficiency and (ii) the heat rejected to the sink.
steps: Formula: eta = 1 - Q2/Q1, so Q2 = Q1(1 - eta).

solved.topic: Coefficient of performance of a Carnot refrigerator
solved.q: A Carnot refrigerator maintains the temperature inside at 270 K while the room temperature outside is 300 K. Find its coefficient of performance.
steps: Given: T2 (cold, inside) = 270 K, T1 (hot, room) = 300 K.
Formula (Carnot refrigerator COP): COP = T2/(T1 - T2).
Calculation: COP = 9 (a dimensionless number, no units).

solved.topic: Coefficient of performance from heat and work (general refrigerator)
solved.q: A refrigerator removes 263 J of heat from the cold chamber for every 40 J of work done on it by the compressor in one cycle. Find (i) the coefficient of performance and (ii) the heat rejected to the surroundings per cycle.
steps: Given: Q2 = 263 J (heat removed from cold body), W = 40 J (work done on refrigerator).
Formula (energy conservation for refrigerator): Q1 = W + Q2.
Calculation: Q1 = 303 J (heat rejected to surroundings).

practice.q: A gas releases 300 J of heat while 500 J of work is done on it. Find the change in its internal energy.
practice.hint: dU = dQ - dW; take dQ = -300 J (heat released), dW = -500 J (work done on gas).

practice.q: 1 mole of an ideal gas is compressed isothermally at 400 K so that its volume is halved. Find the work done by the gas. (R = 8.314 J/mol K, ln2 = 0.6931)
practice.hint: W = nRT ln(V2/V1) with V2/V1 = 1/2, so W = -nRT ln2.
practice.ans: W = -2305 J (work done ON the gas by surroundings)

practice.q: A gas is compressed adiabatically and 250 J of work is done on it. Find the change in internal energy.
practice.hint: dQ = 0, so dU = -dW; work done BY gas is -250 J here.

practice.q: A gas at constant pressure 2 x 10^5 Pa is compressed from 5 x 10^-3 m^3 to 3 x 10^-3 m^3. Find the work done by the gas.
practice.hint: W = P(V2 - V1); V2 < V1 gives negative work.

practice.q: An engine with efficiency 25 percent absorbs 1600 J of heat from the source per cycle. Find the heat rejected and the work done per cycle.
practice.hint: eta = W/Q1 gives W; then Q2 = Q1 - W.

practice.q: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 60 percent when the source is at 750 K. Find the temperature of the sink.
